# Keyboard accessibility fixes for four core Dashboard flows

## Description

This epic makes the four audited core Dashboard flows (project creation,
workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission) fully operable by
keyboard alone, with no focus traps, no unreachable controls, and consistent
visible focus indicators. It addresses every defect enumerated for these flows
in the accessibility audit report that motivated this strategy.

## Scope

- Fix focus loss in modals used by the four audited flows so keyboard focus is
  trapped within open modals and restored to the invoking control on close.
- Make every control in the four audited flows reachable and operable via
  keyboard (tab order, arrow-key navigation where the widget convention
  requires it, Enter/Space activation, Escape to dismiss).
- Apply a consistent visible focus indicator style across all controls in the
  audited flows, matching the platform's design-system focus styling.
- Re-verify each flow end-to-end by keyboard-only walkthrough after the fixes.

Out of scope: screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require,
and flows outside the four audited ones.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each of the four audited flows (project creation, workbench spawn, model
  deployment, pipeline run submission) can be completed start-to-finish using
  the keyboard alone, with no mouse input.
- No focus traps outside open modals, and no controls in the audited flows are
  unreachable via keyboard navigation — every defect listed for these flows in
  the audit report is resolved or explicitly waived with rationale.
- Keyboard focus is moved into each modal when it opens, contained while it is
  open, and returned to the invoking control when it closes.
- Visible focus indicators are consistent (same styling and visibility rules)
  across all interactive controls in the audited flows.
- A keyboard-only walkthrough of each of the four flows is recorded or
  documented as verification evidence.
- Existing Dashboard CI remains green on the changes.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P1): The four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard, with
  no focus traps or unreachable controls.
- HLR-2 (P1): Visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited flows.

# Update and republish accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and accessibility statement)

## Description

This epic updates and republishes the accessibility conformance documentation
to reflect the fixed state of the four core Dashboard flows: the VPAT
conformance statement required by public-sector customers and the product docs
accessibility statement. Both documents are customer-facing deliverables of
this strategy — two public-sector customers require an updated, published
conformance statement before renewal.

## Scope

- Update the VPAT (conformance statement) to reflect the keyboard operability
  and focus-indicator state of the four audited flows after the fixes land.
- Update the product documentation accessibility statement to match the
  current conformance position.
- Republish both documents through the Red Hat docs content process so the
  published versions reflect the fixed state.

Out of scope: documentation of screen-reader semantics or flows beyond the
four audited ones.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The VPAT accurately reflects the keyboard operability and focus-indicator
  conformance of the four audited flows in their fixed state, with no claims
  beyond what the implementation verifies.
- The product docs accessibility statement is updated consistently with the
  VPAT.
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented behavior
  of the four flows (reviewer confirms each documented claim against the
  shipped fixes).
- Both documents are republished; the published conformance statement is the
  version customers can reference for renewal.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P2): The accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and product
  docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect the
  fixed state, with technical review.

## Dependencies

This epic depends on the completion of the keyboard accessibility fixes to the
four core Dashboard flows: the conformance documents describe the fixed state
and cannot be technically reviewed or republished before it exists.

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9017

Keyboard accessibility conformance for core Dashboard flows.

## Triage

Not below-threshold and not docs-only. Although the scope is small and the
audit report enumerates the exact defects (no genuine unknowns), the strategy
spans two architecturally distinct work streams that warrant separate PR
review cycles: Dashboard front-end code fixes (keyboard operability and focus
indicators) and substantive documentation content authoring (VPAT conformance
statement and product docs accessibility statement, republished). Per the
multiple-work-streams escape condition, decomposition proceeds.

## Epic List

| ID | Title | Type | Team | Priority |
|----|-------|------|------|----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 | Keyboard accessibility fixes for four core Dashboard flows | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | P1 |
| RHAISTRAT-9017-E002 | Update and republish accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and accessibility statement) | Implementation (docs-authoring) | RHOAI Documentation | P2 |

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 --> RHAISTRAT-9017-E002
```

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| E001 → E002 | Rule 11 (docs-authoring blocked by all Implementations) | The VPAT and accessibility statement must reflect the fixed state of the four flows; the documentation cannot be technically reviewed or republished until the keyboard fixes land. |

- No Investigation epics. The strategy's Open Questions section is explicitly
  "None — the audit report enumerates the exact defects per flow," so there are

- No konflux-onboarding chain: the Dashboard architecture context confirms the

- No repo-onboarding or license-validation epics: no new repo, no new

- HLR-3 is a docs-authoring epic, exempt from priority inheritance; strategy
  frontmatter priority is Normal → P2.

## Component Mapping

| Strategy component | Canonical component | Notes |
|--------------------|---------------------|-------|
| Dashboard | Dashboard | Direct match; architecture context exists (RHOAI Dashboard, stable, Konflux onboarded). |
| Documentation | Documentation | Direct match in canonical component list. No architecture context file exists, but Documentation is a content component, not a code component — no provisioning/onboarding chain applies. Owning team assigned as RHOAI Documentation. |

All HLRs covered; no orphaned requirements.

## Health Warnings

- **Missing strategy sections** (non-blocking): the strategy has no Impacted
  Teams table, no Dependencies table, no Given/When/Then acceptance criteria,
  and no Non-Functional Requirements section. Epic acceptance criteria below
  were derived from the HLRs, the problem statement, and the audit findings
  described therein; teams should tighten them against the actual audit report.
- **Customer deadline coupling**: two public-sector customer renewals depend on
  the *published* VPAT, not just the code fixes. The documentation epic is the
  customer-facing deliverable, yet it is P2 and serialized behind the code epic.
  This is a scheduling risk, not a priority inversion (the docs cannot precede
  the fixes they describe), but the docs work should be started in draft form
  as soon as the epic scope is clear.

## Tiered Delivery

Not applicable — no external dependency with uncertain timing. The single
Implementation epic delivers the full user-facing value; the docs epic is its
conformance-record deliverable.
